question.problem:
Consider two sets of $18$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{18},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{18}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx}=36,\,{S}_{yy}=27,\,{S}_{xy}=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, ${\sigma }_{y}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the variance of ${y}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{y}^{2} & =\frac{{S}_{yy}}{n},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${S}_{yy}$ is the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${y}_{i}.$

We are given that ${S}_{yy}=27.$ Substituting the given statistic in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{y}^{2} & =\frac{27}{18} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$
